paragraphs.text: For the people according as had been prophesied in Isa 2:2 and Eze 41:1-26, thought this temple should have been more excellent than Solomon's temple, which was destroyed by the Babylonians, but the Prophets meant the spiritual Temple, the Church of Christ.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: That is, go forward in building the temple.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: He exhorts them to patience though they do not see as yet this temple so glorious as the Prophets had declared: for this should be accomplished in Christ, by whom all things should be renewed.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: Meaning Christ, whom all ought to look for and desire: or by desire he may signify all precious things, such as riches, and things like them.

paragraphs.text: Therefore when his time comes he can make all the treasures of the world to serve his purpose: but the glory of this second Temple does not consist of material things, neither can it be built.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Meaning all spiritual blessings and felicity purchased by Christ; Php 4:7.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: That is, the flesh of the sacrifices, by which he means that a thing which of itself is good, cannot make another thing so: and therefore they ought not to justify themselves by their sacrifices and ceremonies: but contrary to this, he that is unclean and not pure of heart, does corrupt those things and make them detestable to God, which otherwise are good and godly.

paragraphs.text: Consider how God plagued you with famine before you began to build the temple.

paragraphs.text: That is, before the building was begun.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: From the time they began to build the temple, he promises that God would bless them: and even though the fruit has not yet come forth, yet in the gathering they would have plenty.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: He exhorts them to have patience, and to remain until the harvest came, and then they would see God's blessings.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: I will make a change, and renew all things in Christ, of whom Zerubbabel is here a figure.

paragraphs.text: By this he shows that there will be no stop or hindrance, when God will make this wonderful restitution of his Church.
